prompt: You add an independent binary enable input to a controller. What must a complete truth table do?

options.text: Add one row for the enable input
options.explanation: Rows describe combinations of all inputs, not individual signals.

options.text: Keep the same rows because enable is only a control
options.explanation: Control inputs still affect which combinations the specification must cover.

options.text: Include both enable values for every existing input combination
options.explanation: Correct. Every old row now has an enable-low and an enable-high case.

options.text: Keep only the combinations that make the output high
options.explanation: A complete truth table also specifies low outputs.

workedExample: Take any previous combination. The new input can be low or high independently, so both cases need a specified output. Matching outputs may later simplify the circuit, but do not remove cases from its specification.
